views.name: users_base
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  users.Id AS Id,
  users.DisplayName AS DisplayName,
  users.Reputation AS Reputation,
  users.CreationDate AS CreationDate,
  users.AccountId AS AccountId
FROM users
views.description: Canonical user rows with primary identity and key profile attributes normalized for reuse.
validated_on: How many posts does the user csgillespie own?
Provide the display name of the user who made the vote No.6347.
counter_examples: For the user with the display name of "Tiago Pasqualini", how many posts did he/she own?

views.name: posts_by_owner
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  posts.OwnerUserId AS OwnerUserId,
  COUNT(posts.Id) AS post_count,
  SUM(IFNULL(posts.AnswerCount, 0)) AS answer_count_sum,
  SUM(IFNULL(posts.ViewCount, 0)) AS viewcount_sum,
  SUM(IFNULL(posts.Score, 0)) AS score_sum
FROM posts
GROUP BY posts.OwnerUserId
views.description: Per-user aggregates of their posts (counts and sums) to support questions about user activity and prominence.
validated_on: Please list the display names of all the users whose accounts were created in the year 2011.
counter_examples: For the user with the display name of "Tiago Pasqualini", how many posts did he/she own?
What is the average of the up votes and the average user age for users creating more than 10 posts?

views.name: user_badges
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  b.UserId AS UserId,
  COUNT(*) AS badge_count,
  MAX(b.Date) AS latest_badge_date
FROM badges b
GROUP BY b.UserId
views.description: Per-user badge counts and latest badge date to support reputation/recognition related questions.

views.name: users_core
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  u.Id AS Id,
  u.DisplayName AS DisplayName,
  u.CreationDate AS CreationDate
FROM users u
views.description: Normalized projection of users with canonical identity, creation date and display name for user-level queries and cohorts.

views.name: comments_core
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  c.Id AS Id,
  c.PostId AS PostId,
  c.UserId AS UserId,
  c.CreationDate AS CreationDate,
  c.Score AS Score,
  c.Text AS Text
FROM comments c
views.description: Row-level comments with user and post linkage and creation date, for comment/cohort filters tied to users.

views.name: users_core_5
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  u.Id AS Id,
  u.DisplayName AS DisplayName,
  u.LastAccessDate AS LastAccessDate
FROM users u
views.description: Canonical projection of users with primary identity columns and normalized date/time fields. Keeps one row per user and exposes fields commonly used for filtering, grouping, and counting.
validated_on: What is the display name of the user who last edited the post "Examples for teaching: Correlation does not mean causation"?

views.name: users_activity_flags
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  u.Id AS Id,
  u.LastAccessDate AS LastAccessDate,
  CASE WHEN u.LastAccessDate IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS has_last_access
FROM users u
views.description: Derived boolean/cohort flags about user activity (e.g., has_last_access, recent_access_before_date). Useful for quickly forming cohorts of active/inactive users without re-deriving null checks each time.

views.name: posts_core
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.Id AS Id,
  p.Title AS Title,
  p.OwnerUserId AS OwnerUserId,
  p.OwnerDisplayName AS OwnerDisplayName
FROM posts p
views.description: One-row-per-post core attributes useful for filtering and joining to owner/user identity. Keeps both canonical owner user id and the stored owner display name from the posts table.
validated_on: Who is the owner of the post titled 'Open source tools for visualizing multi-dimensional data?'

views.name: users_identity
views.body_sql:
SELECT u.Id AS Id,
       COALESCE(p.OwnerDisplayName, u.DisplayName) AS DisplayName
FROM users u
LEFT JOIN posts_core p
  ON p.OwnerUserId = u.Id
GROUP BY u.Id, u.DisplayName
views.description: One-row-per-user identity/display record. Canonical display name for a user (authoritative when OwnerUserId is present).

views.name: post_owner_resolved
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.Id,
  p.Title,
  p.OwnerUserId,
  p.OwnerDisplayName,
  CASE
    WHEN p.OwnerUserId IS NOT NULL THEN u.DisplayName
    ELSE p.OwnerDisplayName
  END AS ResolvedOwnerDisplayName
FROM posts p
LEFT JOIN users u ON p.OwnerUserId = u.Id
views.description: Denormalized view resolving a post's owner to the canonical user display name when OwnerUserId is present, while preserving the post's stored OwnerDisplayName fallback. Useful for queries that want the authoritative owner name plus the stored owner display text.

views.name: posts_row_level
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.Id AS Id,
  p.OwnerUserId AS OwnerUserId,
  p.PostTypeId AS PostTypeId,
  p.AcceptedAnswerId AS AcceptedAnswerId,
  p.CreaionDate AS CreaionDate,
  p.Score AS Score,
  p.ViewCount AS ViewCount,
  p.Title AS Title,
  p.Tags AS Tags,
  p.AnswerCount AS AnswerCount,
  p.CommentCount AS CommentCount,
  p.FavoriteCount AS FavoriteCount,
  p.ParentId AS ParentId,
  p.ClosedDate AS ClosedDate
FROM posts p
views.description: Canonical, cleaned projection of the posts table at one row per post, exposing identifying and commonly filtered/grouped columns (owner, timestamps, counts, parent/accepted answer).

views.name: posts_by_owner_denorm
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.Id AS Id,
  p.OwnerUserId AS OwnerUserId,
  COALESCE(p.OwnerDisplayName, u.DisplayName) AS OwnerDisplayName,
  p.PostTypeId AS PostTypeId,
  p.CreaionDate AS CreaionDate,
  p.Score AS Score
FROM posts p
LEFT JOIN users u ON p.OwnerUserId = u.Id
views.description: Denormalized join of posts to their owner user (one row per post with owner display name included) to simplify owner-based counts and filters.

views.name: posts_core_12
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  posts.Id AS Id,
  posts.Title AS Title,
  posts.OwnerUserId AS OwnerUserId,
  posts.LastEditorUserId AS LastEditorUserId,
  posts.CreaionDate AS CreaionDate,
  posts.LasActivityDate AS LasActivityDate
FROM posts
views.description: One row per post with canonicalized important post columns (IDs, title, owner/last-editor ids, and timestamps). Useful for filtering posts by title and joining to users.

views.name: post_last_editor
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.Id AS Id,
  p.Title AS Title,
  p.LastEditorUserId AS LastEditorUserId
FROM posts p
views.description: Denormalized view mapping each post to its last editor user (if any). Exposes both post key and the linked user id for convenient retrieval of editor attributes.

views.name: posts_rowlevel
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.Id AS Id,
  COALESCE(p.OwnerUserId, NULL) AS OwnerUserId,
  COALESCE(p.Score, 0) AS Score,
  COALESCE(p.Title, '') AS Title,
  COALESCE(p.CreaionDate, p.LasActivityDate, NULL) AS CreationDate,
  COALESCE(p.Tags, '') AS Tags,
  COALESCE(p.PostTypeId, NULL) AS PostTypeId
FROM posts p
views.description: One row per post with canonicalized important post columns and cleaned nulls; exposes owner, score and identifiers used for joins and filters.

views.name: users_rowlevel
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  u.Id AS Id,
  u.Age AS Age,
  u.DisplayName AS DisplayName,
  u.Reputation AS Reputation
FROM users u
views.description: One row per user with canonicalized demographic columns used for filtering (age) and join keys.
validated_on: What is the average score of the posts owned by the user csgillespie?
Which user made a post titled 'Understanding what Dassault iSight is doing?' and how much is the reputation of the user?

views.name: posts_with_owner_denorm
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.Id AS Id,
  p.OwnerUserId AS OwnerUserId,
  p.Score AS Score,
  p.Title AS Title,
  p.CreaionDate AS CreationDate,
  p.Tags AS Tags,
  u.Age AS Owner_Age,
  u.DisplayName AS Owner_DisplayName,
  u.Reputation AS Owner_Reputation
FROM posts p
LEFT JOIN users u
  ON p.OwnerUserId = u.Id
views.description: Denormalized row-level view joining posts to their owner user row; one row per post enriched with owner attributes to support filters like owner age and other user-based cohorts.

views.name: tags_cohort
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  Id,
  TagName,
  ExcerptPostId,
  WikiPostId,
  Count
FROM tags
views.description: One row per tag from the tags table exposing tag id, name and linked post ids (excerpt and wiki) to serve as a tag cohort for filtering and joins.

views.name: posts_core_18
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  posts.Id AS Id,
  posts.Body AS Body,
  posts.Title AS Title,
  posts.Tags AS Tags,
  posts.OwnerUserId AS OwnerUserId,
  posts.CreaionDate AS CreationDate,
  posts.Score AS Score,
  posts.ViewCount AS ViewCount,
  posts.AnswerCount AS AnswerCount,
  posts.CommentCount AS CommentCount,
  posts.FavoriteCount AS FavoriteCount,
  posts.ParentId AS ParentId
FROM posts
views.description: Canonical projection of posts exposing primary identifiers and textual/content fields plus owner and counts. Normalizes column naming inconsistencies from source (keeps original column names) and provides the fields needed to return a post body or join to tags.

views.name: tag_excerpt_posts_join
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  tags.Id AS "tags.Id AS TagId",
  tags.TagName AS "tags.TagName",
  tags.ExcerptPostId AS "tags.ExcerptPostId",
  posts.Id AS "posts.Id AS PostId",
  posts.Body AS "posts.Body",
  posts.Title AS "posts.Title"
FROM tags
JOIN posts ON posts.Id = tags.ExcerptPostId
WHERE tags.ExcerptPostId IS NOT NULL
views.description: Denormalized relation joining tags to their excerpt post (when set). One row per tag that has an ExcerptPostId, exposing tag metadata and the excerpt post's body and identifiers to make retrieving the excerpt content straightforward.

views.name: posts_core_20
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  posts.Id AS Id,
  posts.OwnerUserId AS OwnerUserId,
  posts.Score AS Score
FROM posts
views.description: One row per post exposing owner linkage and core numeric/text attributes used for filtering and aggregation. Keeps raw Score (NULL preserved so AVG semantics work) and OwnerUserId for joins to users.

views.name: posts_by_owner_join_users
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  posts.Id AS Id,
  posts.OwnerUserId AS OwnerUserId,
  posts.Score AS Score,
  users.DisplayName AS OwnerDisplayName
FROM posts
LEFT JOIN users ON posts.OwnerUserId = users.Id
views.description: Denormalized row-level view joining posts to their owner user row; one row per post including owner DisplayName to support queries that filter by user DisplayName without repeating join logic.

views.name: posts_core_22
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  posts.Id AS Id,
  posts.OwnerUserId AS OwnerUserId,
  posts.Score AS Score
FROM posts
views.description: Canonical row-level posts relation with key columns and important numeric/date/text fields normalized (exposes owner reference for joins). Does not filter by any specific score or owner; useful as the base cohort for counts and joins.

views.name: post_with_owner_denorm
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  posts.Id AS Id,
  posts.OwnerUserId AS OwnerUserId,
  posts.Score AS Score,
  users.Id AS UserId,
  users.Age AS Age
FROM posts
JOIN users ON users.Id = posts.OwnerUserId
WHERE posts.OwnerUserId IS NOT NULL
views.description: Denormalized view joining posts to their owner user (when owner exists). Produces one row per post with owner demographic fields for filtering and grouping; keeps raw post score and user age for downstream aggregation.

views.name: comments_rows
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  comments.Id AS Id,
  comments.PostId AS PostId,
  comments.UserId AS UserId,
  comments.CreationDate AS CreationDate,
  comments.Text AS Text,
  comments.UserDisplayName AS UserDisplayName
FROM comments
views.description: One row per comment with core comment attributes, used to filter comments by user, date, and post.
validated_on: Calculate the average view count of each post tagged as 'humor' and list the title and the comment of each post.

views.name: posts_basic
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  Id,
  PostTypeId,
  AcceptedAnswerId,
  CreaionDate,
  Score,
  ViewCount,
  Body,
  OwnerUserId,
  LasActivityDate,
  Title,
  Tags,
  AnswerCount,
  CommentCount,
  FavoriteCount,
  ParentId,
  ClosedDate,
  OwnerDisplayName
FROM posts
views.description: One row per post exposing key post identifiers and raw measures (scores, counts, owner, title, tags).

views.name: comments_with_post_link
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  comments.Id AS "comments.Id",
  comments.PostId AS "comments.PostId",
  comments.UserId AS "comments.UserId",
  comments.CreationDate AS "comments.CreationDate",
  posts.FavoriteCount AS "posts.FavoriteCount",
  posts.Title AS "posts.Title",
  posts.OwnerUserId AS "posts.OwnerUserId"
FROM comments
LEFT JOIN posts ON posts.Id = comments.PostId
views.description: Denormalized relation of comments joined to their posts (one row per comment) to simplify queries that need comment -> post attributes.

views.name: comments_core_27
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  comments.Id AS Id,
  comments.PostId AS PostId,
  comments.UserId AS UserId,
  comments.CreationDate AS CreationDate,
  comments.Text AS Text,
  comments.UserDisplayName AS UserDisplayName,
  comments.Score AS Score
FROM comments
views.description: One row per comment with core identifying and timestamp fields, suitable for filtering by user and creation time or joining to posts.
validated_on: Write the contents of comments with a score of 17.
Name the user that commented 'thank you user93!'

views.name: posts_core_28
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  posts.Id AS Id,
  posts.ClosedDate AS ClosedDate,
  posts.Title AS Title,
  posts.OwnerUserId AS OwnerUserId
FROM posts
views.description: One row per post exposing status and key identifying fields needed to determine if a post is closed and to join back to comments.

views.name: comment_post_link
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  comments.Id AS Id,
  comments.PostId AS PostId,
  comments.UserId AS UserId,
  comments.CreationDate AS CreationDate,
  comments.Text AS CommentText,
  posts.ClosedDate AS Post_ClosedDate
FROM comments
LEFT JOIN posts ON posts.Id = comments.PostId
views.description: Denormalized relation joining comments to their posts so queries can directly access comment and post fields together. One row per comment (keeps comment grain).

views.name: posts_by_owner_30
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  posts.Id AS Id,
  posts.OwnerUserId AS OwnerUserId,
  posts.PostTypeId AS PostTypeId,
  posts.CreaionDate AS CreationDate,
  posts.Title AS Title
FROM posts
views.description: Row-level posts relation exposing owner link and key post attributes so callers can count/filter posts per owner or apply further filters (keeps one row per post).

views.name: votes_rows
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  votes.Id AS Id,
  votes.PostId AS PostId,
  votes.VoteTypeId AS VoteTypeId,
  votes.CreationDate AS CreationDate,
  votes.UserId AS UserId,
  votes.BountyAmount AS BountyAmount
FROM votes
views.description: Raw votes rows (one row per vote) exposing vote identifiers, related post and user references, vote type and timestamps.

views.name: vote_with_user
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  v.Id AS Id,
  v.UserId AS UserId,
  u.DisplayName AS DisplayName,
  v.PostId AS PostId,
  v.VoteTypeId AS VoteTypeId,
  v.CreationDate AS CreationDate
FROM votes AS v
LEFT JOIN users AS u
  ON v.UserId = u.Id
views.description: Denormalized join of votes to the user who cast them, one row per vote including the user's display name; suitable for answering who cast a particular vote and for queries joining vote activity to user attributes.

views.name: posts_by_owner_33
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  posts.Id AS Id,
  posts.OwnerUserId AS OwnerUserId,
  posts.Title AS Title,
  posts.CreaionDate AS CreationDate
FROM posts
views.description: Row-level cohort of posts with their core identifying and ownership columns. One row per post; useful to count or filter posts by owner or other post attributes.

views.name: user_basic_metrics
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  u.Id AS UserId,
  COALESCE(p.post_count, 0) AS post_count,
  COALESCE(v.vote_count, 0) AS vote_count
FROM users u
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT OwnerUserId AS UserId, COUNT(*) AS post_count
  FROM posts
  WHERE OwnerUserId IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY OwnerUserId
) p ON p.UserId = u.Id
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT UserId, COUNT(*) AS vote_count
  FROM votes
  WHERE UserId IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY UserId
) v ON v.UserId = u.Id
views.description: Per-user aggregated measures derived from posts and votes: counts of posts authored (OwnerUserId) and counts of votes cast (UserId). Keeps one row per user and raw counts so downstream queries can compute ratios or additional metrics.

views.name: posts_core_35
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  posts.Id AS Id,
  posts.Title AS Title,
  posts.ViewCount AS ViewCount,
  posts.OwnerUserId AS OwnerUserId
FROM posts
views.description: Canonical row-level representation of posts with primary identifying columns and commonly filtered or returned attributes (no aggregation). Cleans/normalizes column names and exposes title, view count and owner for downstream filtering or aggregation.

views.name: posts_with_comment_counts_and_scores
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.Id AS Id,
  p.Title AS Title,
  p.ViewCount AS ViewCount,
  COUNT(c.Id) AS CommentCount,
  COALESCE(SUM(c.Score), 0) AS Aggregated_Comment_Score
FROM posts p
LEFT JOIN comments c ON c.PostId = p.Id
GROUP BY p.Id, p.Title, p.ViewCount
views.description: One row per post augmented with aggregated comment-level measures (raw counts and sums) and key post attributes. Keeps aggregations at the post row level to support analytics like filtering or ranking posts by comment activity or comment scores.

views.name: posts_by_owner_37
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  posts.Id AS Id,
  posts.Title AS Title,
  posts.ViewCount AS ViewCount,
  posts.OwnerUserId AS OwnerUserId,
  users.DisplayName AS DisplayName,
  users.Reputation AS Reputation
FROM posts
LEFT JOIN users AS users
  ON posts.OwnerUserId = users.Id
views.description: One row per post joined to its owner user (if any). Exposes post identifiers and owner attributes for queries that need user-related filters or joins (e.g., posts by a specific user).
validated_on: Which user made a post titled 'Understanding what Dassault iSight is doing?' and how much is the reputation of the user?

views.name: posts_with_owner_identity
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.Id AS Id,
  p.Title AS Title,
  p.OwnerUserId AS OwnerUserId,
  COALESCE(p.OwnerDisplayName, u.DisplayName) AS OwnerDisplayName,
  p.CreaionDate AS CreationDate,
  p.Score AS Score,
  p.Tags AS Tags
FROM posts p
LEFT JOIN users u
  ON p.OwnerUserId = u.Id
views.description: Denormalized posts with owner user identity fields to support questions that join posts to their authors.

views.name: users_basic_profile
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  u.Id AS Id,
  COALESCE(NULLIF(u.DisplayName, ''), NULL) AS DisplayName,
  u.Reputation AS Reputation,
  u.CreationDate AS CreationDate,
  u.Location AS Location,
  u.AccountId AS AccountId
FROM users u
views.description: Canonical user profile rows exposing key user attributes used for filtering/grouping (basic normalization of nullable display names).

views.name: users_core_40
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  users.Id AS Id,
  users.DisplayName AS DisplayName
FROM users
views.description: Canonical user identity and display fields for joining to other entities.

views.name: comment_authors_denorm
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  comments.Id AS "comments.Id",
  comments.Text AS "comments.Text",
  comments.UserId AS "comments.UserId",
  users.Id AS "users.Id AS User_Id",
  users.DisplayName AS "users.DisplayName"
FROM comments
LEFT JOIN users ON comments.UserId = users.Id
views.description: Denormalized comment rows joined to their author user rows (keeps one row per comment). Useful for queries that need comment text plus author display name and user id.

views.name: posts_core_42
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  posts.Id AS Id,
  COALESCE(NULLIF(posts.Title, ''), NULL) AS Title,
  posts.OwnerUserId AS OwnerUserId,
  posts.PostTypeId AS PostTypeId,
  COALESCE(posts.CreaionDate, posts.LasActivityDate, NULL) AS CreationDate
FROM posts
views.description: One row per post with canonicalized key fields and primary post attributes useful for filtering and joins (keeps original owner reference). Does light cleaning of nullable text/date fields.

views.name: users_identity_43
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  users.Id AS Id,
  users.DisplayName AS DisplayName
FROM users
views.description: User identity rows exposing display name and primary key for joins to posts or other actor tables.

views.name: posts_owner_denorm
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  posts.Id AS Id,
  posts.Title AS Title,
  CASE
    WHEN posts.OwnerDisplayName IS NOT NULL AND TRIM(posts.OwnerDisplayName) <> ''
      THEN posts.OwnerDisplayName
    WHEN users.DisplayName IS NOT NULL AND TRIM(users.DisplayName) <> ''
      THEN users.DisplayName
    ELSE NULL
  END AS resolved_owner_display_name,
  posts.OwnerUserId AS OwnerUserId,
  posts.OwnerDisplayName AS OwnerDisplayName,
  users.DisplayName AS users_DisplayName
FROM posts
LEFT JOIN users ON posts.OwnerUserId = users.Id
views.description: Denormalized view of posts with resolved owner display name: prefer posts.OwnerDisplayName when present/non-empty, otherwise use users.DisplayName for the OwnerName. One row per post.

views.name: comments_by_post
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  comments.Id AS Id,
  comments.PostId AS PostId,
  comments.Text AS Text,
  comments.CreationDate AS CreationDate,
  comments.UserId AS UserId
FROM comments
WHERE comments.Text IS NOT NULL
views.description: All comments with their post link and text; suitable for joining to a post cohort and filtering out NULL texts.

views.name: posts_with_tags_and_basic_metrics
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.Id AS Id,
  p.Title AS Title,
  p.Tags AS Tags,
  p.ViewCount AS ViewCount
FROM posts p
views.description: One-row-per-post projection exposing canonical post identifiers, tag text and basic numeric metrics suitable for filtering and aggregation (no question-specific literals).

views.name: post_comment_denorm_minimal
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  comments.Id AS "comments.Id",
  comments.PostId AS "comments.PostId",
  posts.Id AS "posts.Id",
  posts.Title AS "posts.Title",
  posts.ViewCount AS "posts.ViewCount",
  comments.Text AS "comments.Text"
FROM comments
JOIN posts ON posts.Id = comments.PostId
views.description: Denormalized rows joining posts to their comments. One row per comment linked to its post, exposing post title, post viewcount and the comment text — useful for queries that need post-level metrics alongside each comment row.

views.name: badges_raw
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  Id,
  UserId,
  Name,
  Date
FROM badges
WHERE UserId IS NOT NULL
views.description: One row per badge event as recorded in the badges table, cleaned for NULL user ids. Exposes the badge's id, user, name and date so downstream queries can filter, group, and count badges per user.

views.name: badges_count_per_user
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  user_badges.UserId AS UserId,
  user_badges.badge_count AS badge_count
FROM user_badges
WHERE user_badges.UserId IS NOT NULL
views.description: Pre-aggregated counts of badges per user. One row per user with the raw count of badge rows associated with that user. Does not exclude any specific users beyond NULL UserId filtering handled in the source; keeps the numeric badge_count for thresholding.

views.name: posts_owned_by_user
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  Id,
  OwnerUserId,
  Title,
  ParentId
FROM posts
views.description: One row per post with its owner (author) and basic identifying columns. Useful to filter or join posts by their OwnerUserId.

views.name: posthistory_rows_by_post
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  PostId AS PostId,
  COUNT(*) AS posthistory_count
FROM postHistory
GROUP BY PostId
views.description: Aggregated counts of postHistory rows per post. One row per post indicating how many history entries that post has.

views.name: users_with_views_and_authored_posts_history_stats
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  users.Id AS UserId,
  users.DisplayName AS UserDisplayName,
  users.Views AS Views,
  posts.Id AS PostId,
  ph.posthistory_count AS posthistory_count
FROM users
JOIN posts ON posts.OwnerUserId = users.Id
JOIN posthistory ON posthistory.PostId = posts.Id
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT PostId, COUNT(*) AS posthistory_count
  FROM posthistory
  GROUP BY PostId
) ph ON ph.PostId = posts.Id
WHERE ph.posthistory_count > 0
views.description: One row per user-post pair where the user is the owner of the post and the post has at least one postHistory row; includes the count of postHistory rows for that post. This denormalized view supports checks like 'every authored post that appears in postHistory has exactly one postHistory row' by aggregating per user later.

views.name: badges_row_level
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  b.Id AS Id,
  b.UserId AS UserId,
  TRIM(b.Name) AS Name,
  b.Date AS Date,
  CAST(strftime('%Y', b.Date) AS INTEGER) AS year
FROM badges_raw b
views.description: Canonical, cleaned badge rows exposing key badge attributes and extracted year for time-based filtering. One row per badge.

views.name: badges_by_name_year_cohort
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  Name,
  CAST(strftime('%Y', Date) AS INTEGER) AS year,
  COUNT(*) AS badge_count
FROM badges
GROUP BY Name, CAST(strftime('%Y', Date) AS INTEGER)
views.description: Pre-aggregated counts of badges grouped by badge name and year(Date). Useful for computing shares over years for any badge Name.

views.name: badge_name_total_counts
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  Name AS Name,
  COUNT(*) AS total_count
FROM badges
GROUP BY Name
views.description: Total counts of badges per Name across all years. Useful to compute denominators (total badges for a given Name).

views.name: users_basic_profile_56
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  Id,
  UpVotes,
  Age
FROM users
views.description: One row per user with canonical basic profile fields (clean projection of users table). Exposes fields commonly used in aggregates and filters such as UpVotes and Age.

views.name: user_with_post_counts
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  u.Id AS Id,
  u.UpVotes AS UpVotes,
  u.Age AS Age,
  COALESCE(pbo.post_count, 0) AS post_count
FROM users AS u
LEFT JOIN posts_by_owner AS pbo
  ON pbo.OwnerUserId = u.Id
views.description: Denormalized user row joined with their total post count. One row per user.Id with their UpVotes, Age and post_count. Ready for final filtering and aggregation.

views.name: votes_cleaned
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  v.Id,
  v.PostId,
  v.VoteTypeId,
  v.CreationDate,
  date(v.CreationDate) AS CreationDate_date,
  CAST(strftime('%Y', v.CreationDate) AS INTEGER) AS CreationYear,
  v.UserId,
  v.BountyAmount
FROM votes v
WHERE v.CreationDate IS NOT NULL
  AND strftime('%Y', v.CreationDate) IS NOT NULL
views.description: One row per vote with canonicalized CreationDate truncated to date and the extracted year; excludes votes with NULL or unparsable CreationDate.

views.name: votes_by_year_cohort
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  votes.Id AS Id,
  CAST(strftime('%Y', votes.CreationDate) AS INTEGER) AS CreationYear
FROM votes
WHERE votes.CreationDate IS NOT NULL
views.description: Row-level cohort view that flags the calendar year for each vote for easy year-based filtering and counting. Keeps one row per vote.

views.name: votes_counts_per_year
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  CAST(strftime('%Y', CreationDate) AS INTEGER) AS CreationYear,
  COUNT(*) AS vote_count,
  MIN(Id) AS any_vote_id
FROM votes
WHERE CreationDate IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY CAST(strftime('%Y', CreationDate) AS INTEGER)
views.description: Aggregated counts of votes by calendar year (one row per year). Useful for year-over-year ratios and trends.

views.name: posts_by_owner_61
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  posts.Id AS Id,
  posts.OwnerUserId AS OwnerUserId,
  posts.AnswerCount AS AnswerCount,
  users.DisplayName AS DisplayName
FROM posts
LEFT JOIN users ON users.Id = posts.OwnerUserId
views.description: Denormalized join of posts with their owner user identity (DisplayName) to support queries that pick posts for specific users.

views.name: posts_cleaned
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.Id AS Id,
  p.OwnerUserId AS OwnerUserId,
  CASE
    WHEN p.ViewCount IS NULL THEN 0
    ELSE p.ViewCount
  END AS ViewCount_clean
FROM posts p
views.description: One row per post with cleaned/common post fields: canonical numeric view count (NULL->0) and preserved owner user id for joins.

views.name: post_viewcounts_per_user
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  OwnerUserId,
  SUM(ViewCount_clean) AS TotalViewCount
FROM
  posts_cleaned
GROUP BY
  OwnerUserId
views.description: Aggregated measure: total view count per user computed by summing cleaned post view counts across all posts owned by that user.
